doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Making a living as a musician and teacher
summary: Making a living is a challenge; he teaches at NYU and SUNY Purchase, gives clinics and plays.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: What’s it like to make a living as musicians?

Well it’s challenging but it’s fun and it’s, I mean I’m so into it now, I could probably answer that question better twenty years ago. You know what I mean? But now I mean it’s just a way of life. It’s just the way it is and it’s a lot of fun and it’s a challenge business-wise, it’s a challenge financially, and it’s a challenge to better yourself in the midst of all that. You know what I mean? And to make a living. But I’m lucky I have people, like I say I have pretty good gigs and I teach too, which I like, I’m not a guy that doesn’t like it. Two schools, NYU for twenty-three years and SUNY Purchase for about ten or eleven. And I teach privately too. And I do clinics and concerts, and I still play. You know I have a full schedule. So that’s why I make a living.
Again I’m not sure how to ask this question but I’ll try.
Monk, you’re doing a great job.
